description_en: Tāulī Odār, a small rock shelter, is situated to the north of the village of Michāgāũ on the southern slopes of the Langa Lekh.This particular rock shelter is one among the five caves mentioned by Harka Gurung in the following account: "Near the village were five caves and I dug two but found nothing except some potsherds. They were located on a hill slope and had two sides and a roof of large stone slabs and one had a dimension of 1.37 meter length, 0.91 meter width and 0.80 meter height. Although local version ascribes them to be burial grounds of the earlier Bhotia settlers, I was unable to determine whether these were remains of the early troglodytes or mere megalithic graves."(Gurung 1980, p. 46)The rock formation of Tāulī Odār is relatively shallow, with a depth not exceeding 100 cm and a width of around 200 cm. Currently, there are no evident traces of archaeological artifacts within the rock shelter, nor are there any observable signs of human modifications to the structure. The location of the potsherds mentioned by Gurung is presently unknown.
references: REFERENCES Gurung, Harka. 1980. Vignettes of Nepal . Kathmandu: Sajha Prakashan.
